composition_owner: intergrax/applications/_shared/scaling_wiring.py + production_capacity_wiring.py + production_capacity_governance_wiring.py (capacity); intergrax/applications/_shared/queue_worker_wiring.py + production_queue_resolver.py + host_queue_execution_wiring.py (queue worker); intergrax/runtime/transport/bootstrap.py and intergrax/queueing/bootstrap.py (no-op default registration); intergrax/runtime/task/worker_bootstrap.py (Celery worker app)

risks.text: VERIFIED. build_production_capacity_adapters -> resolve_kubernetes_backend returns an InMemoryKubernetesScaler (seeded nexus-host=2 replicas) when INTERGRAX_KUBERNETES_URL is unset; the Celery 'production adapter' is always an in-memory worker_count record. The PRODUCT preset sets production_adapters_enabled=True, so product hosts without the URL get governed 'successful' scaling against in-memory state and apply_production_scale_probe can pass; nothing in wiring refuses or flags kubernetes_backend=='in_memory' (no consumer of that field outside tests). Architecture doc says missing backend gives 'no silent success' (line 179) and lists the in-memory scaler as CI-only (line 435); tests assert the default is in_memory. Judgment: disclosed in the doc as CI/deterministic, but in conflict with the env-vendor rule (missing mandatory config fails closed) and the 'no silent success' claim; maturity banner (line 10) bounds the claim. See finding f4.

queue_worker_wiring rewrites RABBITMQ/KAFKA backend to CELERY and always builds a Celery app with broker memory://, result backend cache+memory://, task_always_eager=True, independent of production_mode (STRICT hosts legal_application and dispute_sim pass production_mode=True and include_queue_worker). INTERGRAX_QUEUE_BACKEND appears in no doc or test; no test covers the Kafka/RabbitMQ downgrade. Not a distributed queue in that configuration. See finding f5.

Broker queue providers exist under intergrax/queueing/providers/* while integrations/providers/message_bus/* wraps them; the queueing/bootstrap.py docstring still names integrations.providers.kafka/rabbitmq paths that no longer exist (stale doc comment; two homes for broker code).
Scaling/queue composition roots reside in intergrax/applications/_shared, upward from runtime (EQOA-A4-003 class, not re-filed).
